title: Sentence Structures Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the four main sentence structures and what each one does.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language sentence structures walkthrough — simple, compound, complex, compound-complex.
final_note: You learned the four main sentence types and how to identify each in any text.

concepts.def: One independent clause — one main idea
Main clause + at least one subordinate clause
Two main clauses + a subordinate clause
A clause that can stand alone as a sentence
A clause that can't stand alone

walkthroughs.body_html:
A simple sentence has one independent clause: 'She ran.'

Punchy. Direct. Hits hard.

Compound: two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so).

'She ran AND she did not look back.'

Complex: one main + one subordinate.

'Although she was exhausted, she ran.'

The subordinate clause adds nuance.

mcqs.q: 'She ran, and she did not look back' is a:

options: Although it was raining, birds sang.

numericals.q: How many independent clauses are in a SIMPLE sentence?

free_texts.q: What type of clause CANNOT stand alone as a sentence? One word.
